preview: Interview experience of Rozeeta Fernandes for the ICG Intern role at Citi, detailing the unexpected online assessment and three rigorous interview rounds.
content: CITI Interview Experience: Rozeeta Fernandes (ICG Intern) Location: Pune PPT – 1st September, 6pm to 7pm All the students of CS, IT, and circuit branches with a CPI of 6.5 or higher met the eligibility criteria. The company presentation was set for September 1st, 2023, at 6 pm just before it’s online assessment. It is strongly recommended to attend these presentations as having knowledge about the company is crucial, especially for HR rounds. Online Assessment – 1st September, 8pm (1.5 hrs.) The online assessment wasn’t as expected (previous year OAs had CS Fundamentals MCQs, aptitude MCQs + coding questions) and was a shock to many. When we were asked to fill the application for the internship, we had to mention the role we were applying to and were asked to fill in either of the two roles ICG and EIOT in the preferences. I filled in the ICG role as my first preference and the EIOT role as my second preference. The ones who chose EIOT as their role got an OA similar to previous years but the ones who chose ICG were asked coding questions, SQL MCQs, React MCQs, and Angular MCQs (which we were definitely not expecting). Section 1 – DSA: So, this section included 2 coding questions for a total time of 45 mins. 1. This question was an easy one. I was supposed to count how many times a specific character appears in a given string and output the count of the character in the string and print 0 if the character is not found. I was able to pass 12/12 test cases for this. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/program-count-occurrence-given-character-string/ 2. Given the total number of orders placed (say N), a list of N order numbers (positive for vegan pizza, negative for meat pizza), and the number of orders displayed on the screen (say K), I had to find and print the first meat pizza order number for each set of K orders displayed on the screen, or print 0 if no meat orders are displayed. This question was an easy one as well but I probably missed out on something and so could pass 6/18 test cases. At first, I only passed 2 test cases even though I felt like my solution was fine. On making further changes, I could get myself to pass 6 test cases within the time allotted. Section 2 – SQL: This section was easy and consisted of basic SQL questions based on the output, syntax, or particular rules. It was a cakewalk if one had enough practice with SQL. Also, an important point to be noted here is that we couldn’t go back to a previous question that we had visited. The test consisted of 12 MCQs to be solved in 15 mins. There was no negative marking. Section 3 – React: Now, this and the next section were the most unexpected sections for everyone who applied for the ICG role as we expected aptitude questions. I had knowledge in React and had worked with it in quite a few projects, so I did have an idea of it, but many of my friends were either working in the backend or had no idea of React at all. Also, one thing to note here is that there were no questions related to hooks (which are most commonly used) and many of the questions were based on class-based components. The test consisted of 12 MCQs to be solved in 15 mins. There was no negative marking. Section 4 – Angular: This section was unexpected, and I had never worked with Angular before, so I had no idea what to expect. A piece of advice I'd like to share is to look for the most appropriate answer, a strategy we learned during our JEE/CET days, based on the coding knowledge you have gathered so far, rather than randomly selecting options. I had some familiarity with React, so I tried to relate the two and answered accordingly. When faced with something completely unfamiliar, I would simply choose an option and move on to avoid wasting time. This section also had 12 MCQs to be completed within 15 minutes, with no negative marking. Online Interviews – 4th September We were provided with an Excel sheet containing information about our interview times and the names of our interviewers. Round 1 – Technical My interview was scheduled at 11 am, estimated duration of 30 mins, held online on zoom. He started with 'Tell me about yourself'. He asked me a bit about my projects. He then asked me to share my screen and write the code to reverse a linked list in VS Code. He then asked me another DSA question wherein we needed to sort an array of 0s, 1s, and 2s using the 'Dutch National Flag Algorithm'. He then asked to find the second greatest element in an array of numbers that could contain duplicates without using any additional data structures. After this, he asked me some questions on OOP, DBMS, OS such as what is threading, some MongoDB queries, CPU speed, core, etc. Since the time exceeded, he asked me to orally answer 2-3 questions like what is 40% of 79. Round 2 – Technical I was asked to introduce myself and explain my projects using the STAR method. He asked a MongoDB query and how I would handle merge conflicts when working in a team project, and why Node.js was used. He asked about shortest path algorithms in a graph ('Dijkstra’s Algorithm' and 'Bellman Ford'), real-life applications of stacks, and a simple profit and loss question. Round 3 – HR The HR round felt more like a casual conversation. He asked me to introduce myself, inquired about my goals and aspirations, the role I aspire to work in, and my location in Pune. Resources: For DSA, 450 DSA, LeetCode, GFG, Take U Forward, Aditya Verma. For OS and DBMS, Gate Smasher’s playlists. InterviewBit for OS, DBMS, OOP, React, and HR questions.
